statements.hypotheses: Every integer n≥1, compact convex K⊂R^n with nonempty interior and K=−K; polar at 0.
conclusions: Equality iff K is an invertible linear image of a Hanner polytope.

statements.hypotheses: n≥1; even proper lower-semicontinuous convex φ:R^n→R∪{+∞}; 0<∫exp(−φ)<∞.
n≥1; η_i=exp(−V_i)dx full-dimensional origin-symmetric log-concave probabilities; proper lsc convex V_i; essentially continuous densities.
d≥1; nonzero, pairwise nonproportional real rows spanning (R^d)*; lens of Lemma 3.1; A,S,Σ_X as (21),(22),(26).
n≥1; origin-symmetric equality body K; Q=K°; B=K⊕_1[−1,1], C=Q×[−1,1]; X∈int B, 0≠ξ=(q,a), T=p_C(ξ).
conclusions: There are ≤n+1 rows c_i∈Q×{−1,1}, α_i≥0 summing to T with ξ=∑α_i c_i.
One Y is feasible for every h∈C and attains c_i·Y=λ(c_i·X) for all selected rows.
The selected cost is no larger than any finite positive C-representation of ξ.

statements.hypotheses: n≥1; origin-symmetric equality body K; Q=K°.
conclusions: Every triple in (R^n,p_Q) has a metric median.

proofPassages.scope: Lemma 2.1 formulas (5)–(7), Lemma 2.2 recursive Hanner attainment and polar closure.
Lemmas 3.1–3.2, convex lens construction, uniform vertical coordinate, λ concavity and uniform endpoint scaling.
Lemma 4.1 hypotheses; Stokes sublevel comparison; homogeneous flux, phase invariance and Cauchy–Binet normalization.
Lemma 5.1 high inverse powers and radial rescaling; finite-measure upper Fatou; Lemma 5.2 extra boundary constraints null.
Proposition 6.1 probability/simplex identity, disjoint interiors, exact deficit; Corollary 6.2 polar approximation sandwich.
Proposition 7.1 all three parts; product neighborhoods, bounded witnesses, degenerate bases and common witness quantifiers.
Proposition 8.1 support-function median construction including saturated cases; Lemma 8.2 arbitrary radii; Theorem 8.3 and Proposition 8.4.
